I rewrote the propers/verified.md row 'Psalm to first reading' from the Nova Vulgata (hash 9c9c78c4 for Isaias and e508ed1c for Psalmorum, both re-verified) and the readings page (hash 7e0b44c0). The refrain, Ps 80(79):4 'Deus, converte nos', asks God to turn us. Isaiah 63:17b 'Convertere propter servos tuos' asks God to return. The shared petition is Ps 80(79):15 'Deus virtutum, convertere', which the US psalm renders adverbially. The reception tie is Jerome on Isaiah 64:7 (Vulgate; Lectionary 64:6), who uses Ps 79:4 on the hidden face (PL 24 cols. 648-649, which I read on page images). Aquinas [85023] glosses 'convertere de ira ad misericordiam' with Ps 89:13 and cites 'converte nos' separately from Lamentations 5:21. A sweep of scope.md, interpretations.md, context.md, the instance manifest and the shared owner found no other sentence that rests on the false identity. scope 3.3 and Reading 3's psalm row now state the distinction.

summary: I repaired the research review's three blocking findings and cleared all four advisories. (1) Jerome is now credited with the comments that Bede copies onto Mark 13:32-33. I read them on the page image of the registered Migne PL 26 PDF, fetched whole with a matching hash: Commentarii in Matthaeum IV, Matthew 24:36 and 24:42-43, cols. 181-182, PDF p. 98. The PDF is bound with its own deferred disposition. Bede is kept for his own comments on 13:34-37. (2) The propers/verified.md row on the psalm and the first reading now keeps two petitions apart: the refrain (Ps 80:4) asks God to turn us, while Isaiah 63:17b asks God to return. The petition they share is at Ps 80:15, and the reception tie runs through Jerome (PL 24 col. 649) and Aquinas ([85023]). (3) I regenerated the chronology record and annotations; the only change is the verified.md fingerprint.
